caption: NASA astronaut Kate Rubins at the Combustion Integrated Rack (CIR) holding the chamber insert for the Advanced Combustion via Microgravity Experiments (ACME) suite of experiments during 3 Feb. 2021 preparations for the next investigation.
what_it_represents: Astronaut reconfiguring hardware at the CIR facility on the ISS.
qualitative_trends_and_observations: Shows physical scale and hardware configuration of CIR and chamber insert.

caption: ACME chamber insert used within the CIR facility.
what_it_represents: Component layout of ACME chamber insert including mass flow controllers, PMT array, thermocouple rake, burner, camera, radiometer array, mesh electrode, and retracting hot-wire igniter.
legend_information: Labeled components: PMT array, Thermocouple rake, 3 Mass Flow Controllers, Burner, Camera (color, analog), Radiometer array, Electrode (mesh), Igniter (hot-wire, retracting).
qualitative_trends_and_observations: Illustrates the integration of sensors and controls on the chamber axis.

caption: Gas-jet flames shown at different scales: (a) composite overlay of three dilute methane coflow flames as a function of the matched fuel/coflow velocity, (b) example of the effect of the electric field strength on the flame size where the downstream mesh was negatively charged.
what_it_represents: Visual appearance of lifted dilute methane coflow flames and electric field compaction effects.
experimental_conditions_represented: Matched fuel/coflow velocity; electric field potential up to 10 kV
qualitative_trends_and_observations: Flames become more compact as electric field potential becomes increasingly negative.

caption: Low-momentum flames shown at different scales: (a) pure ethylene BRE flame where the burner is illuminated from the left in red, (b) inverse flame encompassing the porous spherical burner, with an oxygen/nitrogen mixture flowing from the burner into an ethylene/nitrogen atmosphere, (c) false-colored image of a diluted hydrogen flame, revealing the burner and glowing ceramic fibers for Thin-Filament Pyrometry.
what_it_represents: Dome-shaped BRE flame, inverse spherical flame, and TFP fiber pyrometry image.
experimental_conditions_represented: Low-momentum microgravity conditions; porous burner configurations
qualitative_trends_and_observations: Demonstrates stable low-momentum burning and spherical flame configurations.

caption: Appearance of a cool flame, in intensified imaging, after the hot flame quenches in a normal-flame test with diluted n-butane.
what_it_represents: Transition from hot flame quenching due to radiative heat loss to cool flame appearance over time (60.87 s to 65.65 s).
legend_information: Time stamps from 60.87 s to 65.65 s
experimental_conditions_represented: CFI-G normal-flame test with diluted n-butane
qualitative_trends_and_observations: Hot flame quenches around 61.30-61.74 s, followed by appearance of a much smaller cool flame from 63.04 s onwards.
